briefs.headline: India's bank-led rally fails Monday's risk-off test: NIFTY -1.75%, financials retreat, Tata Steel–APL Apollo transaction reprices; crude relief remains conditional

Source archive and sector/stock snapshots refreshed 09:28-09:30 UTC but sector and stock completed bars remain 20 November: Monday technical breakouts cannot be assessed. Sector leadership and priced event-risk: stale 20 Nov private-bank +8.40pp and PSU-bank +8.24pp 3m relative returns versus NIFTY now contradicted by Monday bank losses; stored 23 Nov 09:28 UTC December Fed +25bp YES 92.5¢ (+2pp versus 22 Nov 20:26 snapshot), $426,443 24h betting volume and $824,935 liquidity. These are price and betting data, not institutional sector flows. No fresh verified NSE 23 Nov gross FII/DII, NSDL sector allocation, AMFI, TIC or CFTC numeric figures. Evidence supports risk-off session, not a proven structural bear regime.

stories.title: Fed Collins favors gradual additional rate hikes
stories.whatHappened: 14 Nov: Boston Fed President Susan Collins said steady, modest additional rate rises best manage uncertainty; Vice Chair Jefferson separately stressed inflation data rather than a fixed path.
whyItMatters: A higher US risk-free rate raises discount rates for long-duration Indian equities and increases external dollar funding costs.
A gradual path is less disruptive than a large surprise move, but sticky inflation reduces the scope for rapid easing.

stories.proxies: Indian NBFCs, banks, REITs, exporters and IT valuations

stories.caution: Statements are not a policy decision; a softer inflation print or falling yields would weaken tightening thesis.

stories.title: India October goods deficit reaches one-year high
stories.whatHappened: 13 Nov official-data reporting: merchandise deficit $39.88bn in October versus $30.21bn September; imports $89.35bn, exports $49.47bn, petroleum imports $22.82bn and gold $5.51bn.
whyItMatters: A wider merchandise deficit increases external dollar demand and can pressure the rupee when oil is elevated.
Record exports partially offset import pressure; services surplus matters for the overall current account.

stories.proxies: IT/pharma exporters may benefit from INR weakness; airlines, paints and chemicals vulnerable to imported costs
stories.whatCouldChange: Monthly trade balance, services balance, oil import bill and INR/USD
stories.caution: Festival gold imports can be temporary; merchandise deficit is not current-account deficit.

Mine threats can raise freight, war-risk insurance and refined-product costs even when crude supply is abundant.

briefs.headline: Foreign capital is rotating toward India, but sector positioning and the global risk backdrop are not uniformly bullish
briefs.executiveSummary: The clearest verified shift is renewed foreign institutional buying in India's broad equity market after October withdrawals. Indian bank and auto stocks led price gains, although the latest fortnightly published FPI-sector data showed prior investment interest in IT/telecom rather than confirmed November financial-sector inflows. Oil-price moderation helps some importers, but shipping/geopolitical and monetary-policy risks remain. A global AI capex/valuation debate adds potential rotation pressure without proving an AI downturn.
